title: Amazon Open-Sources 5 Decider v2 Decision Models, Long-Horizon Reasoning Accuracy Soars, Reshaping the Foundation of Agent Decision-Making

content_html:
At a time when AI Agents are moving from “single-point tools” to “executors of complex tasks,” developers face a common pain point: when models face long-duration, multi-step complex tasks, they often fall into a decision-making black hole of “logical breakdown” or “blind overconfidence.” What we need is no longer a generator that merely produces expansive text, but a “decision-making brain” with high accuracy, high confidence, and the ability to precisely manage long-horizon context.

Recently, Amazon’s Strands Agents team officially released the **Strands Decider v2 series decision models**, offering a highly sincere open-source solution to this chronic industry problem. This series is deeply built on Google’s Gemma4 architecture and includes five models of different scales, from E2B to 31B. It is fully open-sourced under the permissive Apache-2.0 license, and the weights are already available on Hugging Face, allowing developers to seamlessly integrate local deployment and secondary development.

Core breakthrough: tempered by 17.5 million samples, long-horizon reasoning no longer “loses the thread”

Compared with v1, Decider v2 has undergone a comprehensive reconstruction of its underlying architecture and introduced up to **17.5 million high-quality training samples**. Feeding data at this scale directly breaks through the performance bottleneck that previous decision models faced with long-text inputs, significantly improving the model’s understanding and judgment in complex contexts.

Official benchmark data shows that across six authoritative public text benchmarks, the **Strands Decider v2 31B model achieved an average score of 82.1**, a leap forward compared with the 70.0 score of the 26B-A4B model in the v1 series. Even more impressive, not only text reasoning but also its decision-making performance in multimodal tasks such as images and video has been significantly enhanced. Even the smaller E4B version shows a visible leap in accuracy in specific lightweight scenarios.

Industry insight: why are “decision models” more critical than “generative models”?

In the current AI ecosystem, generative models are responsible for “diverging creativity,” while decision models are responsible for “converging logic.” When enterprises try to build automated workflows, intelligent code review, or complex business scheduling systems, a model’s “confidence” and “accuracy” directly determine the life or death of the business. A single incorrect decision route can cause the entire automation chain to collapse.

Amazon’s choice this time to build Decider v2 on Gemma4 and fully open-source it sends a clear signal: **competition in AI infrastructure is shifting from “competing on parameter scale” to “competing on decision reliability in vertical scenarios.”** By providing a rich matrix from 2B to 31B, Amazon enables developers of different sizes to find the optimal solution that balances “inference cost” and “decision quality,” truly lowering the barrier to entry for enterprise-grade Agents.

Developer dividend: another “blood transfusion” for the open-source ecosystem

For developers troubled by the high cost of closed-source APIs and data privacy concerns, the full open-sourcing under the Apache-2.0 license is undoubtedly a shot in the arm. Whether used as an independent routing decision hub or fine-tuned and embedded into existing RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) workflows, Decider v2 provides a high-starting-point, trustworthy foundation.

When AI Agents no longer make decisions by “shooting from the hip,” but instead proceed step by step based on rigorous logic and high-confidence reasoning, we are one big step closer to truly reliable “digital employees.” Amazon’s open-sourcing this time is not only a sharing of technology, but also a powerful underpinning for the industrialization of AI Agents.
